title: Software Engineer roadmap
description: From first programs to shipping reliable software in a team.

provenance.method: Stages follow the order in which each skill is normally needed on the job; targets for skills the career already requires come from that career's requirement rows, and the rest are set by Capabilio to be reachable by a final-year student.
provenance.notes: Original tree. Designed from first principles and the canonical skill taxonomy; not derived from any third-party roadmap.

nodes.title: Programming foundations
nodes.description: Write and debug small programs with confidence.

nodes.title: Tools of the trade
nodes.description: Work the way software teams work: version control and the command line.

nodes.title: Data structures
nodes.description: Store and organise data so programs stay simple and fast.

nodes.title: Algorithms and problem solving
nodes.description: Turn a problem into an efficient procedure.

nodes.title: Object-oriented design and quality
nodes.description: Model software clearly and keep it correct as it changes.

nodes.title: Data and persistence
nodes.description: Keep data correct, queryable and fast.

nodes.title: Services and systems basics
nodes.description: Build networked services and understand what runs beneath them.

nodes.title: System design and delivery
nodes.description: Design for scale and ship work as part of a team.

nodes.title: Core constructs
nodes.description: The building blocks every program is made of.

nodes.title: Craft
nodes.description: Habits that make code something others can use.

nodes.title: Version control
nodes.description: Track, share and combine changes.

nodes.title: Working environment
nodes.description: Comfort on the command line and with the web's protocol.

nodes.title: Linear structures
nodes.description: Ordered collections and the cost of using them.

nodes.title: Lookup and hierarchy
nodes.description: Fast lookup, ordering and tree-shaped data.

nodes.title: Techniques
nodes.description: Reusable ways of solving problems.

nodes.title: Reasoning about cost
nodes.description: Compare approaches before writing code.

nodes.title: Modelling with objects
nodes.description: Represent the problem domain in code.

nodes.title: Quality
nodes.description: Make changes safe.

nodes.title: Relational data
nodes.description: Tables, queries and guarantees.

nodes.title: Choosing a store
nodes.description: Know what else exists.

nodes.title: Building services
nodes.description: Interfaces other programs can rely on.

nodes.title: What runs beneath
nodes.description: How the machine runs your code.

nodes.title: System design
nodes.description: Design beyond a single machine.

nodes.title: Delivering as a team
nodes.description: Turn needs into shipped software.

nodes.title: Variables and Control Flow
nodes.description: Declares and updates variables and uses conditions and loops to control what a program does. Every other topic rests on this, so it should feel automatic.

nodes.title: Functions and Scope
nodes.description: Breaks code into functions with clear inputs and outputs and understands where a name is visible. Small, well-named functions are the unit of reuse in every codebase.

nodes.title: Error Handling and Debugging
nodes.description: Finds the cause of a failing program with a systematic method and handles errors without hiding them. Engineers spend much of their time finding out why code does not do what they expected.

nodes.title: Programming fundamentals in practice
nodes.description: Writes correct, readable programs using the basic building blocks of a language. Brings the basics together: the career expects fluent, correct code.

nodes.title: Git Fundamentals
nodes.description: Tracks changes with commits, inspects history and undoes mistakes safely using Git. Nearly every team shares code through Git.

nodes.title: Branching and Merging
nodes.description: Works on parallel lines of development and combines them, resolving conflicts correctly. Parallel work needs branches and calm conflict resolution.

nodes.title: Code Review Practice
nodes.description: Gives and receives pull-request feedback that improves correctness and readability. Review is how teams catch mistakes and share knowledge.

nodes.title: Version control in a team
nodes.description: Tracks and shares changes to code so a team can work together safely. The career expects confident everyday use of version control.

nodes.title: Command Line Basics
nodes.description: Navigates the file system and combines shell commands to inspect and transform files. Servers, build tools and many developer tools are driven from the shell.

nodes.title: Linux
nodes.description: Works comfortably on a Linux system from the command line. Most production software runs on Linux.

nodes.title: HTTP Fundamentals
nodes.description: Understands requests, responses, methods, headers, status codes and how the web uses them. Almost every service you build or call speaks HTTP.

nodes.title: Arrays and Strings
nodes.description: Stores and transforms sequences of values and text, and knows the cost of common operations on them. The most common structures in everyday code and in interviews.

nodes.title: Linked List Operations
nodes.description: Builds and manipulates singly and doubly linked lists, including insertion, deletion and reversal. Teaches pointer-style thinking that carries into trees and graphs.

nodes.title: Stacks and Queues
nodes.description: Uses last-in-first-out and first-in-first-out structures and recognises the problems they suit. Appear in parsing, scheduling and search.

nodes.title: Hash Maps and Hashing
nodes.description: Uses key-value lookup in constant expected time and reasons about collisions and load. Constant-time lookup is the most used performance tool in practice.

nodes.title: Trees and Binary Search Trees
nodes.description: Represents hierarchical data, traverses trees and keeps ordered data in a binary search tree. Hierarchies and ordered data are everywhere, from file systems to databases.

nodes.title: Heaps and Priority Queues
nodes.description: Maintains the smallest or largest item efficiently and applies it to scheduling and top-k problems. Needed for scheduling, top-k and shortest-path problems.

nodes.title: Data structures in practice
nodes.description: Chooses and builds the right structure for the data and the operations a program needs. The career expects you to pick the right structure without hesitation.

nodes.title: Sorting and Searching Algorithms
nodes.description: Chooses and implements common sorting and searching methods and compares their running time. The standard examples for reasoning about efficiency.

nodes.title: Recursion and Backtracking Patterns
nodes.description: Solves problems by breaking them into smaller copies of themselves and exploring choices with undo. Natural for trees, graphs and search problems.

nodes.title: Dynamic Programming Patterns
nodes.description: Solves overlapping-subproblem tasks by defining a state, a recurrence and an order of evaluation. A common test of problem-solving depth.

nodes.title: Greedy Algorithm Design
nodes.description: Builds a solution from locally best choices and judges when that is provably enough. Useful when a locally best choice is provably enough.

nodes.title: Algorithm Analysis
nodes.description: Estimates how running time and memory grow with input size using Big-O reasoning. Lets you reject a slow design before building it.

nodes.title: Graph Algorithms
nodes.description: Models relationships as graphs and solves problems with traversal and shortest-path methods. Models networks, dependencies and routes.

nodes.title: Algorithms in practice
nodes.description: Designs step-by-step procedures that solve problems correctly and efficiently. The career expects solid algorithmic judgement.

nodes.title: Problem Solving
nodes.description: Breaks an unfamiliar problem into parts, tries approaches and checks the result. Reading a vague problem and breaking it down is the core engineering skill.

nodes.title: Classes and Encapsulation
nodes.description: Models things as classes, hides internal state and exposes a small, clear interface. The basis of structuring larger programs.

nodes.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
nodes.description: Reuses behaviour through inheritance and composition and writes code that works on many types. Lets you extend behaviour without rewriting code.

nodes.title: Object-Oriented Design Patterns
nodes.description: Recognises and applies common object-oriented solutions such as factory, observer and strategy. A shared vocabulary for common designs.

nodes.title: Object-oriented programming in practice
nodes.description: Organises programs around objects that combine data and behaviour. The career expects you to design with objects confidently.

nodes.title: Code Quality and Refactoring
nodes.description: Improves the structure of working code without changing behaviour, guided by readability and tests. Maintainable code is what lets a team keep moving.

nodes.title: Unit Testing Practice
nodes.description: Writes small automated tests for one behaviour at a time, with clear arrange-act-assert structure. Fast tests make every later change safer.

nodes.title: Test-Driven Development
nodes.description: Drives a design by writing a failing test first, making it pass, then cleaning up. Builds the testing habit and sharpens design.

nodes.title: Software testing in practice
nodes.description: Checks that software does what it should, and keeps checking as it changes. Brings unit, integration and system testing together.

nodes.title: SQL Query Basics
nodes.description: Retrieves and filters rows with SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT. Most applications store their data in a relational database.

nodes.title: SQL Joins
nodes.description: Combines tables with inner and outer joins and reasons about row counts after a join. Real data lives in several tables.

nodes.title: Relational Database Design
nodes.description: Models data in related tables with keys and constraints that keep it consistent. A good schema prevents whole classes of bugs.

nodes.title: Indexing and Query Performance
nodes.description: Speeds up queries with indexes and reads query plans to find what is slow. Slow queries are a common production problem.

nodes.title: Transactions and ACID
nodes.description: Keeps data correct under concurrent change using transactions, isolation levels and constraints. Keeps data correct when many things happen at once.

nodes.title: Database systems in practice
nodes.description: Explains how database systems store, query and protect data. The career expects you to understand what the database does for you.

nodes.title: NoSQL Databases
nodes.description: Uses non-relational stores such as documents and key-value databases and knows when they fit. Know when a document or key-value store fits better.

nodes.title: REST API Design
nodes.description: Designs resource-oriented HTTP interfaces with consistent naming, status codes, errors and versioning. Clean interfaces let teams build independently.

nodes.title: Authentication and Authorization
nodes.description: Separates who a user is from what they may do, and protects endpoints with sessions or tokens. Getting access control wrong is a serious failure.

nodes.title: Integration Testing
nodes.description: Tests how components work together, including databases and external services, with controlled test data. Checks that parts work together, not only alone.

nodes.title: Computer Networks
nodes.description: Explains how machines communicate across a network and what can go wrong. Explains latency, failures and why requests time out.

nodes.title: Processes and Threads
nodes.description: Explains how programs run as processes and threads and how the operating system schedules them. Explains how your program shares the machine.

nodes.title: Concurrency Basics
nodes.description: Writes code that shares data safely between threads using locks and avoids races and deadlocks. Concurrent code is easy to get subtly wrong.

nodes.title: Operating systems in practice
nodes.description: Explains how an operating system manages processes, memory and files. Knowing what the OS does makes performance and bugs less mysterious.

nodes.title: Scalability Basics
nodes.description: Reasons about load, bottlenecks and the trade-offs of scaling a service up or out. Understanding bottlenecks comes before adding servers.

nodes.title: Caching Strategies
nodes.description: Decides what to cache and where, and handles staleness and invalidation. One of the most effective and most error-prone performance tools.

nodes.title: System design in practice
nodes.description: Designs the parts of a larger system and how they fit and scale together. Expected for mid-level roles and increasingly for entry interviews.

nodes.title: Requirements and User Stories
nodes.description: Turns a need into clear, testable requirements and acceptance criteria. Building the right thing starts with understanding the need.

nodes.title: Agile Delivery
nodes.description: Plans and ships work in short iterations, uses feedback and keeps a working product at each step. Most teams ship in short iterations.

nodes.title: CI/CD
nodes.description: Automates building, testing and releasing software. Automated build and test pipelines are standard practice.

nodes.title: Software engineering in a team
nodes.description: Builds software as a team: planning, design, quality and delivery. The career expects you to work effectively on a team codebase.
